incident-bot: Paging SRE oncall: high error rate + oscillating fallbacks detected for smart-routing group 'eu-mlpool'. severity: P1 :rotating_light:
Lena: seeing a ton of 503s and timeouts for a handful of high-traffic customers in eu-west. metrics spike at 10:12 UTC.
Lena: frontend shows repeated reroutes: eu-west -> us-east -> eu-west in ~500ms intervals, requests getting dropped after 3 attempts.
Devon: looking at smart-routing logs, policy evals show destinations alternating between model_variant=quant128 and model_variant=fp16_v2. quant128 does NOT support tool_calling, many requests require tool calls -> fallback to fp16, then fp16 sometimes hits capacity and routes back to quant128. loop.
Kai: confirmed. compatibility matrix incorrectly marked quant128 as toolcall-capable for eu region due to stale onboarding entry. that causes routing policy to prefer quant variant then fallback.
Lena: affected customers report missing external-data lookups (tool calls) — end-user visible failures.
Devon: stack traces show failure mode: "tool_calling not implemented" from quant backend then routing decision triggers fallback. also seeing context-limit rejects for some long prompts (quant model trained with 2048 vs app expects 4096) -> additional incompat.
Lena: TL;DR policy mislabel + model capability mismatches -> oscillating fallback loop -> high latency + 5xx for toolcall workflows. customer impact: 3 enterprise tenants, ~20% API failure rate since spike.
Kai: immediate mitigations: 1) open circuit-breaker for 'eu-mlpool' smart-routing to stop auto-failover, 2) pin affected tenant routes to fp16_v2 until matrix fixed, 3) reduce routing decision TTL to avoid thrash.
SRE Pager: can you apply circuit-breaker now?
Lena: applying now, running the config change.
oncall-bot: deploy started by Lena — change: smart-routing.circuit_breaker.eu-mlpool=true (request id 0a1b2c)
Lena: circuit breaker engaged. monitor shows error rate dropping within one minute.
Devon: pinning tenant route for tenant=tac_inc to model=fp16_v2 with a temporary override:
```
POST /admin/route_override
{
  "tenant": "tac_inc",
  "route": "model:fp16_v2",
  "expires": "2026-03-15T12:30:00Z"
}
```
Lena: override applied for the three affected tenants. latency normalizing but still some residual 503s as in-flight requests finish.
Kai: I'm going to roll a hotfix to the onboarding compatibility script so new entries cannot mark quant variants as toolcall-capable unless validated. will also add a guard that checks context_length >= requested_context for pinned tenants.
Product - Maya: we need a customer-facing postmortem once stable. please capture which queries failed and whether data was lost.
Devon: collecting traces and constructing a prompt-set to repro. preliminary root cause: compatibility matrix allowed mismatched flags (tool_calling:true, max_context:4096) for quant128; actual binary lacks the hook and has max_context=2048. upstream model metadata ingestion missed these fields for quant variants.
Lena: current status: circuit-breaker ON, tenant pins applied, customer impact dropping to <2% failures.
Kai: next steps: 1) roll hotfix to metadata ingestion (dev patch) 2) add a CI check that validates model binary capabilities vs catalog metadata 3) reconcile compatibility matrix entries for all quant variants 4) schedule follow-up oncall rotation for longer tail.
SRE Pager: handing off to next oncall Kai for 2-hour watch. Kai, you're primary.
Kai: ack, I'll monitor dashboards and keep Product looped. log of useful queries and traces saved to /mnt/sre/incident-1728882024.
Product - Maya: ping me once you have customer impact numbers, I'll coordinate comms.
Lena: leaving this with Kai. leaving detailed notes:
- root cause: stale metadata allowed incompatible quant variant to be treated as toolcall-capable and 4k context; led to oscillating fallbacks under load
- mitigation: circuit-breaker + tenant pin + metadata ingestion hotfix in progress
- follow-ups: CI gate, catalog reconciliation, customer outreach, add telemetry alert for mismatched capability failures
Kai: will also add alert rule: if routing oscillation count > 10/min trigger auto-circuit and page.
Devon: saved a snippet that helped detect the loop:
```
# quick query to find oscillation pairs
SELECT request_id, path, route_history, timestamp FROM routing_logs
WHERE route_history LIKE '%quant128%fp16_v2%quant128%' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 100
```
Lena: thanks all. will update incident doc and start the timeline. handing off to Kai. :white_check_mark:
Kai: handoff accepted. I'll post follow-ups and timeline to #postmortems once we confirm root cause and customer impact.
